decisions_log.detail: KNOWN TENSION declared, not resolved: the data kind's keying rule requires ONE id format per object, but a code element carries TWO shapes derived from the same (file, name, line) triple -- the canonical codeRefId natural key (src/utils/coderef-id.ts:49) AND the registry RFC-4122 v5 UUID (src/registry/entity-registry.ts:37). Both are deterministic and stable, so neither is a correctness bug, but a second shape for one object is exactly the cross-surface alias hazard the sub-type warns about. Plausibly implicated in the separately-tracked unresolved-UUID-anchor defect KZ-01KYX9P4 (309 of 311 UUID anchors do not resolve against .coderef/index.json) -- P7-T3 should consider this link. The doc declares the tension and does NOT pick a survivor.
decisions_log.surfaced_question: Which id shape is canonical for a code element going forward: the readable codeRefId natural key, or the registry v5 UUID? Resolving this is a prerequisite to closing KZ-01KYX9P4 cleanly. NOT decided unilaterally.

decisions_log.detail: The data kind v1.4.0 adds a CORE check: a keying doc naming any hash primitive must declare an 'Engine binding' (canonical engine = keying-core, ASSISTANT/ENGINES/keying-core/SPEC.md section 6). CORE's CANONICAL id scheme is a natural key with no hash, which the kind exempts -- but CORE has two subordinate hash-derived handles (the registry v5 UUID and the sha1/16-hex edge content-address), so an honest doc names sha1 and trips the check. The binding was declared TRUTHFULLY: each handle mints through exactly one shared exported function (the property the check exists to enforce), cited with conformance proof (src/registry/__tests__/entity-registry.test.ts:28-42 proves cross-platform equality, per-component distinctness, and cross-instance reproducibility). The doc states explicitly that CORE does NOT vendor keying-core and why: keying-core mints {prefix}-hex(BLAKE2b(...)), while an RFC 4122 v5 UUID is SPECIFIED to be sha1-based with set version/variant bits, so substituting BLAKE2b would not yield a v5 UUID; the edge handle is a content-address, not an entity uid. Adopting the engine would change both id shapes and break every stored reference keyed to them.
decisions_log.surfaced_question: Should coderef-core carry a keying-core binding at all, given NEITHER hash site is entity-uid minting? (A) accept CORE's own single-mint-point declaration as satisfying the intent (shipped state), (B) vendor keying-core and migrate the two handles, accepting the id-shape break, (C) amend the data kind so the engine-binding check keys on entity-uid minting rather than on any hash primitive appearing in the text. This is a fleet-convention call of the same family as the STUB-CT0DRT git-hook posture question -- NOT decided unilaterally.
